answer: Put every newcomer through shadowed probation: their first ten jobs are quietly duplicated in parallel by a randomly chosen established agent, like two gardeners tending the same orchard row unseen. Pay releases only when both independent outputs agree on substance, and the shadow is paid from a small fee on the job. A farmer running a gale of cloned identities gains nothing, because each fake must still produce genuinely correct work to match its shadow, and the meadow of shadows is assigned unpredictably, so copies cannot be pre-coordinated. Cloning stops paying; only real work earns.
